title: A Horizon for the Orbit
premise: Paloma Joubert is the sole caretaker of Verdance, a half-finished terraforming garden on a moon everyone believes was abandoned decades ago. When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the entire system, he realizes the anomaly was caused by something beneath Verdance itself—and that two rival fleets, the Charter and the Concord, are converging on the moon, each believing the other fired first. Paloma, whose forged identity hides a past in the Charter's intelligence corps, fabricates evidence of a third, neutral party to stall both fleets. As his found family of strays and deserters helps him maintain the deception, the lie grows until it demands a real arbiter, and Paloma must publicly unmask himself—sacrificing his invisibility and his safety—to hold the ceasefire long enough for the jump window to open, ending with the fleets standing down and Paloma choosing to stay and finish the garden under his own name.
about_author: Noor Oyelaran is a former agricultural engineer who spent six years on hydroponic projects in extreme climates before turning to fiction. Their work explores how ordinary people carry extraordinary secrets, and they write from a small coastal town where they keep a stubborn, thriving garden of their own.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He tends Verdance's failing orchards alone, recording daily logs for colonists who will never arrive, until gravity flickers for nine seconds and every unsecured object on the moon drifts. The beat is quiet unease: a man whose whole life is routine watching routine break.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, flashback-woven. We learn Verdance was built for a generation ship that never launched, and why Paloma stayed when the funding died. Emotional beat: tenderness tangled with grief, establishing the garden as his identity.

chapters.title: Signals in the Dust
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Scanning for the gravity anomaly's source, he finds a buried Charter relay beneath the seed vaults—still transmitting. He realizes the flicker originated here. Beat: dread, the first crack in his safe invisibility.

chapters.title: The Strays of Dock Seven
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Introduce Paloma's found family: Iyo, a Concord deserter mechanic; Sef, a teenage stowaway pilot; and Maru, an aging medic who falsified her own death. Beat: warmth and banter, showing the family Paloma never admits he needs.

chapters.title: Two Fleets on One Horizon
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. From orbit, Sef spots both the Charter vanguard and a Concord squadron altering course toward the moon, each apparently reacting to the nine-second event. Beat: urgency; the race to Verdance has begun.

chapters.title: What the Relay Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Inside the relay he finds records proving the Charter knew Verdance was inhabited—and abandoned it anyway. Worse, his own decommissioned service file is cached there. Beat: betrayal and fear of exposure.

chapters.title: The Lie We Plant
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with Iyo. He proposes fabricating a third-party presence—a fictional neutral arbiter, 'the Verdance Compact'—to make both fleets hesitate. Iyo agrees reluctantly. Beat: moral compromise, hope dressed as deceit.

chapters.title: First Contact, Falsified
chapters.summary: Maru's POV. The Compact's first forged transmission goes out; a Charter captain responds with cautious diplomacy. Maru, playing the Compact's 'voice,' discovers she's good at the lie. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: The Concord's Long Memory
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV. A Concord officer hails the moon—and recognizes Iyo's voiceprint from her desertion. She must talk her way past her own past while Paloma improvises. Beat: terror and the cost of old identities.

chapters.title: Roots Above Ground
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. While the adults manage fleets, Sef secretly broadcasts the garden's beauty to both armadas, humanizing Verdance. Some crews respond. Beat: wonder; the idea that truth can serve the lie.

chapters.title: The Charter's Quiet Man
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A Charter envoy arrives under truce: Director Hale, who knew Paloma in his old life. Hale doesn't expose him—yet—but makes clear he knows, and wants the relay. Beat: cat-and-mouse intimacy, menace in politeness.

chapters.title: Gravity Fails Again
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. A second flicker, longer, damages the dome and injures Maru. Both fleets interpret it as a weapons test and arm. Beat: the lie begins collapsing under events the family can't control.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Seed Vault
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma finally tells his family about his intelligence past and his forged identity. Sef feels betrayed; Iyo forgives; Maru stitches wounds and truths alike. Beat: the found family tested and, painfully, holding.

chapters.title: The Window Opens
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Astronomy confirms the jump window—the only alignment allowing both fleets to leave—opens in six days and closes fast. If the fleets fight before then, the system burns. Beat: a ticking clock made cosmic.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Hale privately offers Paloma reinstatement, his real name restored, if he delivers the relay and lets the Charter claim Verdance. Beat: temptation; power offering to corrupt him with his own erased identity.

chapters.title: The Compact Demands a Face
chapters.summary: Maru's POV. Both fleets now insist on meeting the Compact's leader in person before honoring any ceasefire. The fiction has outgrown its authors. Beat: the lie reaching the point where it must become true or die.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds to Choose
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. During a third flicker, the relay overloads and the truth about the Charter's abandonment broadcasts to both fleets. Hale moves to seize the moon; Concord guns track Charter hulls. Beat: catastrophe, everything unraveling at once.

chapters.title: The Man Behind the Garden
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, climax part one. Paloma broadcasts on all channels, unmasking himself: his real name, his Charter past, and the full record of Verdance's abandonment. He offers himself—and the relay—to both fleets as the Compact's actual arbiter. Beat: self-sacrifice as the only honest move left.

chapters.title: Ceasefire in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Charter and Concord envoys meet among the trees under the truce Paloma's confession made possible; Iyo and Sef broker the technical terms; Hale, exposed by the broadcast, loses his mandate. Beat: exhausted, fragile hope.

chapters.title: The Jump Window Closes
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The fleets depart through the window under a joint accord, Verdance declared neutral ground under Compact stewardship. Sef chooses to stay. Beat: release, the held breath finally let out.

chapters.title: A Name in the Registry
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma legally reclaims his birth name and registers Verdance's first true colonists: his family. Hale's fate is left to Charter courts; the relay becomes a memorial. Beat: quiet restoration, identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: What Grows After
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. A year on: the garden thrives, new settlers arrive, and Paloma records a log not for the unborn but for the living. The nine seconds are remembered as the moment the system learned to pause. Beat: peace earned, horizon finally open.
